title: fix(types): the six held public blocks refuse the content channels no renderer reads (objectui#10872 batch 5)
body:
Part of #10872
Clause-②: yes

Batch 5 of objectui#10872: the content-channel narrowing of the six held public blocks, by the objectui#9256 method. The blocks are `action:button`, `action:icon`, `action:group`, `action:menu`, `element:definition-list` and `element:repeater`, the six arms batch 4 armed by reference (PR objectui#11180). The card stays open for the rest of its remainder: `record:line_items`, which has no spec row, and the flat-props / envelope-key batch.

## The defect

Batch 4 gave each of these blocks an arm, and each arm took `BaseSchema`'s channels as they were.
- `{ "type": "action:group", "children": [ … ] }` parsed green on both faces: `safeValidateSchema` (which `objectui validate` runs) and `StrictAnyComponentSchema`. The same held on all six.
- No renderer of the six reads the node's `children` or `body`, and `SchemaRenderer` strips both keys out of the props it spreads. So the child list rendered nothing, and nothing warned at render time.
- A flat `body` was already refused (objectui#6771). Its message said "Did you mean `body` → `children`", which pointed the author at the key that did nothing.

## The change

- **`packages/types/src/zod/public-blocks.zod.ts`, the six arms only.** Each arm declares `children` as a by-name refusal and restates `body` with the same guidance. That is two `retirementTombstone` members fed one `neitherContentChannelGuidance` string, both kept members: the construct the nineteen objectui#9256 arms already use. There is no new helper and no copy of one. The message names what the block renders instead, which is where the content goes:
  - `properties.actions` for `action:group` and `action:menu`;
  - `properties.items` for `element:definition-list`;
  - `properties.label` and `properties.icon` for the two buttons, whose label and icon are their whole content;
  - nothing for `element:repeater`, which has no content channel. Its message says so.

  The module docblock's "The content channels" section is updated to match: its paragraph said these six carry no channel refusal.
- **`packages/types/src/__tests__/held-block-content-channels-10872.test.ts` (new, 115 tests).** It covers both faces:
  - each channel is refused with `invalid_type` at its own path;
  - the message names the block, the method, and the channel (or says there is none), and never "Did you mean";
  - one string feeds both the issue message and the `.describe()` metadata;
  - every value is refused;
  - each tombstone is a member of the arm;
  - a positive control per block: its `properties` node parses on both faces;
  - nested in a `page`, the block parses without a child list and is refused with one;
  - the installed spec's `PageComponentSchema` refuses a node-level `children` on each of the six (see below).
- **Two text follow-ons that the arms made false (see Deviations).** In `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`, the six `EXCLUSIONS` reason strings and their comment said "minus the objectui#9256 channel refusals". The matching paragraph in `packages/types/src/zod/README.md` said "They carry no content-channel refusal".
- **`.changeset/10872-held-block-content-channels.md`.** It declares `'@object-ui/types': minor` (below).

## Zone 2: the PM's mechanism assumptions, each measured

1. **No renderer reads `children` on the six: CONFIRMED, by a runtime probe per block.** This is a one-off probe and was not committed. It ran the real `SchemaRenderer` against the real registry. Each registered renderer was wrapped so that the `schema` it receives is a Proxy logging every `get` / `has` / `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` of `children` and `body`. Each node was rendered without, and then with, a marker child (`element:text`).
   - Results, per block: 0 reads of either key; the DOM was byte-identical with and without the child; the marker never rendered; 0 console warnings or errors either way.
   - The states covered were closed and opened (the `action:group` dropdown and `action:menu` opened: their items were visible), `action:group` inline, an empty definition list, and a repeater painting two rows from an adapter.
   - **Positive control:** `page:card` with the same child rendered the marker, and its wrapper logged 4 reads. The instrument sees a reader when one exists.
   - A `body` leg gave the same result: 0 reads, identical DOM.
   - The parser tier's `not-a-container` warning (objectui#9910) fires on all six. `page:card` draws none.
   - A second instrument agrees. A TypeScript compiler-API census ran one program for `@object-ui/components`, where all six register, on a built tree: the workspace dependencies resolved to `dist/index.d.ts`, with 0 diagnostics in the closure. It listed every `.children` / `.body` read in the in-package import closure of the modules that register the six (64 files). That came to 29 reads, all in `src/ui/*` Shadcn primitives, each destructuring React `children` from a Radix or HTML props type. There were 0 reads in the six renderers' modules, `readProps` or the action helpers.
   - The overlap PR objectui#11185, which edits the four `action:*` renderers, adds no read of either key. Its added lines were grepped on its head `05d9cfdfa`, and the `body` hits there are fetch request bodies in tests.
   - **No block is excluded from the narrowing.**
   - These readings were taken once, and nothing in the tree re-derives them. The committed pin pins the validator's answer, not the renderers'.
2. **What the installed spec does with a node-level `children`: it REFUSES it.** On `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, `PageComponentSchema.safeParse({ type, id, children })` returns `unrecognized_keys` naming `children` for each of the six, with the message "Unrecognized key(s) on this page component: `children`. Before ADR-0089 D3a these were dropped silently …". The same node without `children` passes. The spec's page component has no node-level `children` at all. **So this is not a second dialect: the tombstones bring objectui's face into line with the spec.** The new pin's last block re-reads this from the installed spec, so a spec that starts accepting the key turns red there.
3. **The content channels: PARTLY as guessed.** Each 17.5.0 row was read, and none of them declares `children` or `body`.
   - `action:group` and `action:menu`: the channel is `actions`.
   - `element:definition-list`: the channel is `items`.
   - `action:button` and `action:icon`: no child channel. Their content is the `label` and `icon` members, and the message names those.
   - `element:repeater`: **no content channel**. Its rows print `titleField` / `fields` values of the queried record, with no template or slot, and its message says so.
4. **The objectui#9256 construct applies to by-reference arms without a second helper: CONFIRMED.** These arms are `BaseSchema.extend({ type, properties: propsBag(…) })`, the same shape as the nineteen objectui#9256 arms. The same two helpers apply unchanged. `neitherContentChannelGuidance`'s fixed sentence states a TypeScript type-checker measurement, a `SchemaRenderer` strip and a `not-a-container` warning. Each of those was measured true for the six, as recorded in item 1.
5. **`NAMESPACED_REFUSED_AT_TYPE` does not move: CONFIRMED.** `git diff 37d1662 -- packages/cli/src/__tests__/registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts` is empty, and that test is green at head. No type joins or leaves refused-at-type. Draft PR objectui#11069's hunks are untouched, and that PR shares no file with this one.

## Semver: `minor`, and why nothing published breaks

`minor` follows the objectui#9256 narrowing precedent: this repo's version policy forbids `major` in any changeset. But the narrowing is **not breaking against the last release**, and that was measured:
- `npm view @object-ui/types` gives `latest` = `17.6.0`, the same as `packages/types/package.json`.
- The published 17.6.0 `dist` carries no `ActionButtonBlockSchema` and no `action:button` literal.
- Its own `safeValidateSchema` refuses every one of the six types, with and without `children`, with `invalid_union` at `type`. A `page` passes as a control.
- The batch-4 changesets are still pending in `.changeset/`, so batch 4 and this batch ship in one release. Across that release the accept set only widens.

This refines the claim's `Clause-②` reason ("narrows the published accept set"). `Clause-②: yes` is kept as the claim directs.

## Tests and gates, at head `79b4668ae` (clean tree), with exit codes captured before any pipe

- `os-verify-lock` chain: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` gives "✓ dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete (136 emitted files verified)".
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` gives "Test Files 286 passed (286) / Tests 6726 passed (6726)".
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over five files gives "Test Files 5 passed (5) / Tests 321 passed (321)". The files are `packages/cli/src/__tests__/registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts`, `scripts/__tests__/check-handler-key-read-sites.test.ts`, `examples/schema-catalog/test/safe-validate-corpus-6318.test.ts`, `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` and `packages/cli/src/__tests__/validate-union-arm-selection.test.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` runs `tsc --noEmit`, `tsconfig.examples.json` and `tsconfig.test.json`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new pin, and the chain ends with `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- The `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/types^...' build` step the order names selects an empty closure, because `@object-ui/types` has no workspace dependency. pnpm answers `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT` (exit 1): nothing ran, and that is not a red build.
- Node gates, all exit 0:
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: "4 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)";
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK, 9549 files;
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: "0 new citation(s)";
  - `pnpm check:handler-key-reads`: "OK 139 arm(s) … 57 judged";
  - `pnpm check:changeset-claims`;
  - `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`;
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`;
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs`;
  - `pnpm check:installed-pin-claims`;
  - `pnpm check:spec-symbols`;
  - `pnpm check:test-path-roots`;
  - `pnpm check:doc-types`;
  - `pnpm check:doc-fences`;
  - `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`;
  - `node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`: "43/43 packages compile their tests";
  - `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`: "107 candidate test files, all adjudicated". This batch adds no markdown reader.
- The self-scan for control bytes over the five changed files returns 0 lines.
- ESLint, narrowed: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the three changed TS files counted 3 files, 0 errors and 2 warnings. Both warnings are `no-explicit-any` in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`, already there and outside this diff's hunks.
  - Population: the three `.ts` files in the diff. The other two changed files are markdown.
  - Invariance: `eslint --print-config` shows no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is declared to CI.

**Ablation (one-off, trap-guarded, via `ablation-replace.mjs` in objectstack):** the whole six-arm region at HEAD (12954 bytes) was replaced by the same region at base `37d1662` (6196 bytes), which is exactly the batch-4 arms.
- The tool reported: anchor 1 → 0; blob `370bd3e00e51` → `da78bcf5a4f5`.
- With the mutation in place, the new pin gave **"Tests 66 failed | 49 passed (115)"**, the direction and count predicted before the run:
  - the 12 `children` refusals;
  - all 24 message cases;
  - the 12 one-string cases;
  - the 6 every-value `children` cases;
  - the 12 nested cases.
- It stayed green, as intended, on the population count, the members (`BaseSchema` declares both keys), the positive controls, the spec block and the `body` refusal code.
- Restore: "blob == HEAD (370bd3e00e51) and `git diff HEAD` is empty".
- The pin imports the arms by relative source path, so no `dist` leg applies.

**NOT MEASURED:**
- `check:doc-snippets`: PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2). It needs 34 packages built. This diff edits no fenced block: the two changed lines of `packages/types/src/zod/README.md` are prose paragraphs outside any fence, so they cannot move that gate's verdict. Declared to CI.
- `check:readme-exports`: exit 1, "431 self-import(s) could not be judged", every one because another package's `dist` is not on disk. It reports 0 findings under `packages/types` (built) and "0 wrong-path, 0 fabricated". Declared to CI.

## In-flight overlap, re-read at this head

- **PR objectui#11125** (head `8f9bb76f6`) shares `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of this branch with its head exits 0.
- **PR objectui#11185** (head `05d9cfdfa`) shares no file with this PR, and adds no channel read (Zone 2, item 1).
- **PR objectui#11069** (head `a11f73347`) shares no file with this PR. Its strict-face wiring agrees with this change, because both faces refuse.

## Deviations (declared)

- **Surface widened by one file, `packages/types/src/zod/README.md`**, one paragraph and one sentence. They stated the opposite of this change: that these six carry no content-channel refusal. AGENTS.md #2 requires a package README to follow the code, and batch 4's claim amendment ratified the same README paragraph as an additive fix. The file is not in this claim's file surface. It sits in commit `b4be1d8` together with the census rows and the changeset, so dropping it means reverting that file's hunk, not the commit.
- `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: only the six rows this batch moves, plus their comment. Text only: the census reads reasons for presence and length, not for content.

## Acceptance notes

- **carrier: this card's flat-props / envelope-key batch.** Noted, not filed. The spec's `PageComponentSchema` also refuses a node-level `children` on the four `page:` containers (`page:card` was measured in the same probe: `unrecognized_keys`, `children`). objectui accepts one there, and its renderer does read it. That is the node-level spelling of a spec container's `properties.children`, the same class as the flat keys that batch holds, and it is not this batch's to decide.

Governed surfaces: none. This PR does not touch any governed surface: `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` reports "NOT GOVERNED — 5 path(s) checked".
